chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to me from his father. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-'Abdi, from al-A'mash, from 'Abaya ibn Riba'i, from Abdillah ibn Abbas.

He said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) one day, weeping and saying: To Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: What is it, O Ali? So 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah! My mother Fatima bint Asad has died. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) wept, then said: May Allah have mercy on your mother, O Ali. Know that if she was a mother to you, she was indeed a mother to me. Take this turban of mine and take these two robes of mine, and shroud her in them. And instruct the women to perfect her funeral bath. Do not carry her out until I come, for I will personally attend to her affairs.

He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came after a short while. Fatima, the mother of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), was brought out, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prayed over her a prayer the like of which he had never prayed over anyone before her. Then he recited forty takbirs over her. Then he entered her grave and lay down in it. No groan nor movement was heard from him. Then he said: O Ali! Enter. O Hasan! Enter. So they entered the grave. When they finished what was needed, he said to them: O Ali! Come out. O Hasan! Come out. So they came out. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) crawled until he was at her head.

Then he said: O Fatima! I am Muhammad, the Master of the Children of Adam, and I do not say this boastfully. When Munkar and Nakir come to you and ask: Who is your Lord? Say: Allah is my Lord, Muhammad is my Prophet, Islam is my religion, the Quran is my Book, and my son is my Imam and my wali. Then he said: O Allah! Make Fatima steadfast in the firm word. Then he came out of her grave, sprinkled handfuls of dirt on her, then struck his right hand upon his left and shook them off. Then he said: By Him in Whose hand is Muhammad's soul! I have heard Fatima clapping my right hand against my left.

'Ammar ibn Yasir stood up to him and said: May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! You have prayed over her a prayer the like of which you have never prayed over anyone before her. He said: O Abu al-Yaqzan! She deserves that, for she is from me. She had many children from Abu Talib — their goodness was abundant while ours was little. She would feed me while leaving them hungry, clothe me while leaving them naked, and groom me while leaving them disheveled. He said: Why did you recite forty takbirs over her, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Yes, O Ammar — I turned to my right and saw forty rows of angels, so I recited a takbir for every row. He said: And your lying down in the grave — why did we hear no groan nor movement from you? He said: Indeed, people will be raised naked on the Day of Resurrection, and I did not cease beseeching my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to resurrect her modestly covered. By Him in Whose hand is Muhammad's soul! I did not leave her grave until I saw two lamps of light at her head, two lamps of light at her hands, and two lamps of light at her feet. And the two angels assigned to her grave will seek forgiveness for her until the Hour rises.

key_terms.إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُ: The Quranic inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un (2:156) — the phrase of patience recited at news of death or calamity
key_terms.الْقَوْل الثَّابِت: Al-qawl al-thabit — the firm word; refers to Quran 14:27, the steadfastness of the believer in answering the grave's questions
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَة: Takbira — the proclamation 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greatest); in funeral prayers, additional takbirs are said
key_terms.سَتِيرَة: Satira — modestly covered/veiled; the Prophet's supplication for Fatima bint Asad to be resurrected covered on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.سَيِّد وَلَد آدَم: Sayyid walad Adam — the Master of the Children of Adam; a well-known title of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.مُنْكَر وَنَكِير: Munkar and Nakir — the two angels who question the deceased in the grave
key_terms.وَلِيّ: Wali — guardian, patron, spiritual authority; here used for the Imam

ai.seo_question: What happened at the funeral of Fatima bint Asad, mother of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the death of Fatima bint Asad, mother of Imam Ali (AS), and the extraordinary honors the Prophet (SAWW) bestowed upon her. The Prophet wept at the news, shrouded her in his own garments, performed a funeral prayer over her unlike any he had prayed before (with forty takbirs corresponding to forty rows of angels), personally entered and lay in her grave, instructed her in the answers to the angels' questions, and interceded for her to be resurrected modestly covered. The account demonstrates the profound spiritual station of Fatima bint Asad, who had been like a mother to the Prophet himself, raising him after the death of Amina.
